phase.title: Execution Trust Foundation
phase.goal: 建立可信的任务执行、运行时隔离、版本恢复与监控基础，让平台先具备结果可信、失败可诊断、问题可回滚的底座。
requirements: REQ-003 强化平台可靠性与隔离能力，包括容器化子站点、版本回滚、监控告警和更稳定的任务执行能力
success_criteria: 任务执行结果能够真实反映预览重启、部署与关键后处理是否成功，失败不会再以成功态误导用户。
子站点运行与任务执行具备更明确的隔离边界，关键高风险路径不再默认依赖宿主级权限。
版本快照、回滚与基础监控成为可依赖能力，出现异常时可以定位、恢复并给出清晰状态。

entries.title: Roadmap: NextProject
entries.summary: Phase 1 is Execution Trust Foundation and Phase 2 depends on it.

entries.title: Architecture Constraints
entries.summary: Keep api -> services layering, keep async work in tasks/services, preserve legacy compatibility while tightening behavior.

entries.title: Validation Rules
entries.summary: Backend changes need targeted pytest coverage, and user-facing flows need success and failure-path verification.

architecture.summary: Phase 1 should harden execution truth, legacy control-path auth, runtime isolation, rollback integrity, and observability without rewriting the modular monolith.
findings: backend/services/task_service.py is the execution truth boundary for status, logs, provider output, and preview restart.
backend/main.py still exposes legacy /api/* control paths through get_legacy_user(), creating a privileged compatibility surface.
backend/services/site_service.py and docker-compose.yml currently leave host-level execution paths enabled by default.
backend/services/version_service.py already owns snapshot/rollback and is the right seam for rollback hardening.
backend/core/metrics.py is the existing observability entry point and should be extended instead of adding a new telemetry path.

implementation.summary: The smallest viable decomposition is to first persist execution identity and access control primitives, then make status/result propagation and metrics reflect those primitives.
findings: enqueue_task() dispatches Celery jobs but does not persist celery_task_id even though AgentTask has a celery_task_id column.
run_develop_task() marks SUCCESS even when preview restart fails, and deploy_task() marks SUCCESS immediately after restart_site().
task_logs_websocket() accepts any task id and replays logs without auth or ownership checks.
version_service.rollback_to_version() destroys the live root and untars directly without checksum or staging validation.
useTaskLogs.ts builds a raw websocket URL today, so authenticated websocket access needs an explicit token transport.

integration.summary: Phase 1 spans DB-backed task truth, Celery worker boundaries, websocket fan-out, legacy compatibility routes, filesystem-backed snapshots, and the default runtime compose topology.
findings: Task truth crosses database state, websocket publish, provider output artifacts, and preview runtime restart results.
Legacy /api/* and /api/v2 coexist, so risky legacy routes must be tightened without removing compatibility paths.
Websocket log streaming depends on task_service.publish() -> Redis pub/sub -> websocket_manager broadcast.
Rollback integrity depends on site root replacement and subsequent site restart inside site_service.
Isolation work touches both process startup in site_service and host privileges granted by docker-compose.yml.

risk.summary: The highest-risk paths are privileged legacy config/task routes, unauthenticated log streaming, raw shell startup, host Docker socket access, and destructive rollback without validation.
findings: backend/main.py exposes /api/config and many legacy task/provider routes with default-admin behavior through get_legacy_user().
backend/api/v2/websocket.py exposes task logs and status for any task id without auth or ownership checks.
backend/services/site_service.py executes start_command through sh -lc, which preserves shell injection semantics.
docker-compose.yml mounts /var/run/docker.sock into main-service and celery-worker by default.
backend/services/version_service.py removes the live site tree before validating restore success.

planning_constraints: Keep legacy /api and /api/v2 compatibility unless an endpoint is explicitly tightened.
Prefer minimal direct changes and targeted tests.
